name: Denisova Cave eyed needle
description: An intact eyed bone needle from Main Chamber horizon 11.2 at Denisova Cave bears wear the excavators interpreted as evidence of use. The small eye suggests a fine thread.

impact.note: Needles from one cave; fine sewing let that group make fitted clothing for the cold, a new ability, but no descent from this site is shown.

date.label: Approximately 40,000 cal BP (38,050 BCE)
date.basis: Approximate archaeological context; calibrated BP values use 1950 as reference.

events.statement: An intact eyed bone needle was recovered in horizon 11.2 of the Main Chamber at Denisova Cave. The excavation team reported microscopic traces of wear.

evidence.supports: A 2024 archaeological review lists an eyed-needle date of approximately 40,000 cal BP at Denisova Cave.

evidence.locator: pp. 72–75, especially pp. 72–74 and Figs. 1–2 (same PDF pages)
evidence.supports: Records the needle’s exact chamber and horizon and describes polish and wear on the object. An estimated thread size is inferred from the eye.

events.caveats: The approximate age refers to the archaeological context. The 50,300 ± 2,200 radiocarbon-year determination elsewhere in the excavation report is from a cut-marked bone in the East Chamber. The needle's user, thread material and sewn product are unknown.

earliest_record.rationale: The excavated Main Chamber needle anchors this case. The date represents an approximate archaeological context.

caveats: The approximate age refers to the archaeological context. The 50,300 ± 2,200 radiocarbon-year determination elsewhere in the excavation report is from a cut-marked bone in the East Chamber. The needle's user, thread material and sewn product are unknown.

research.note: The 2016 excavation report supplies horizon 11.2, Main Chamber, and use-wear. Gilligan et al. give the approximate 40,000 cal BP site attribution. A later account by the excavator gives 40–45 ka BP for Main Chamber layer 11; the dates are contextual and no tighter date for this object is assigned here.
